title: Discovery and Structure-Activity Relationships of Pyrrolone Antimalarials
authors: Murugesan, Dinakaran; Mital, Alka; Kaiser, Marcel; Shackleford, David M.; Morizzi, Julia; Katneni, Kasiram; Campbell, Michael; Hudson, Alan; Charman, Susan A.; Yeates, Clive; Gilbert, Ian H.
reference: Discovery and Structure-Activity Relationships of Pyrrolone Antimalarials | Murugesan, Dinakaran; Mital, Alka; Kaiser, Marcel; Shackleford, David M.; Morizzi, Julia; Katneni, Kasiram; Campbell, Michael; Hudson, Alan; Charman, Susan A.; Yeates, Clive; Gilbert, Ian H. | Journal of Medicinal Chemistry (2013), 56(7), 2975-2990
experimental_procedure: (E)-Ethyl 5-[[2,5-dimethyl-1-(4-methylsulfinylphenyl)pyrrol-3-yl]methylene]-2-methyl-4-oxo- 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. The vessel was placed in a microwave oven and heated (180 °C, 15-20 min) under microwave irradiation (0-400 W at 2.45 GHz). After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). Phosphorous oxychloride (0.5 mL, 6 mmol) was added dropwise to stirred ice-cooled DMF (12 mL) under a N2 atmosphere. The mixture was then allowed to warm to room temperature over 15 min, a solution of the pyrrole (6a-r) (1 mmol) in DMF (5 mL) added and the mixture heated at 100 °C for 3 h under a N2 atmosphere. After cooling, 30% aq NaOH was added dropwise to pH 10.0 and the resulting precipitate was filtered, washed several times with water and dried in vacuo to give the corresponding formyl derivative 7a-r (80-95%), which was generally used without further purification. To a solution of ethyl 5-methyl-3-oxo-1,2-dihydropyrrole-4-carboxylate (3) (1.0 equiv) in absolute ethanol (3 mL) was added 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl/substituted aryl-3-formylpyrroles (7a-r) (1.0 equiv) and potassium hydrogen sulphate (0.2 equiv). The reaction mixture was heated at 70-80 °C for 3 h, resulting in the formation of a yellow precipitate. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure. A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (570 mg, 5 mmol), aniline (558 mg, 6 mmol), and amberlite IR 120 (200 mg) was stirred at room temperature under solvent-free conditions for 18 min. After completion of reaction, as monitered by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the reaction mixture was diluted with diethyl ether and filtered to recover the catalyst. experimental_procedure: Scheme 1. General Synthetic Approach to Pyrrolonesa A. General procedure for the microwave-accelerated synthesis of 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrroles(6). 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. The vessel was placed in a microwave oven and heated (180 °C, 15-20 min) under microwave irradiation (0-400 W at 2.45 GHz). After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). B. General Procedure for the synthesis of formyl pyrroles (7a-r). Phosphorous oxychloride (0.5 mL, 6 mmol) was added dropwise to stirred ice-cooled DMF (12 mL) under a N2 atmosphere. The mixture was then allowed to warm to room temperature over 15 min, a solution of the pyrrole (6a-r) (1 mmol) in DMF (5 mL) added and the mixture heated at 100 °C for 3 h under a N2 atmosphere. After cooling, 30% aq NaOH was added dropwise to pH 10.0 and the resulting precipitate was filtered, washed several times with water and dried in vacuo to give the corresponding formyl derivative 7a-r (80-95%), which was generally used without further purification. Scheme 1. General Synthetic Approach to Pyrrolonesa Compound 7s, yield 95%.

authors: Devi, Aarti; Shallu; Sharma, M. L.; Singh, Jasvinder
reference: Paal-Knorr pyrrole synthesis using recyclable amberlite IR 120 acidic resin, a green approach | Devi, Aarti; Shallu; Sharma, M. L.; Singh, Jasvinder | Synthetic Communications (2012), 42(10), 1480-1488
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure. A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (570 mg, 5 mmol), aniline (558 mg, 6 mmol), and amberlite IR 120 (200 mg) was stirred at room temperature under solvent-free conditions for 18 min. After completion of reaction, as monitered by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the reaction mixture was diluted with diethyl ether and filtered to recover the catalyst. The ether layer was washed with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine solution, dried (anhydrous Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by silica-gel column chromatography (eluting with 20% ethyl acetate in hexane). Pure product N-phenyl-2,5-dimethylpyrrole (846 mg) in 99% yield. The recovered catalyst was washed with 5% diluted HCl and dried prior to reuse. The IR spectrum of the recovered catalyst was identical to that of the commercially available catalyst, which was reused for further reactions (six times) without loss of activity. All the compounds are known and were identified by comparison with those of the authentic samples. 3-(2,5-Dimethyl-pyrrol-1-yl)benzoic Acid (Entry 9). Yield 97%. Mp 145-146°C. 1H NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 2.10 (s, 6H), 5.71 (d, 2H), 7.76 (m, 2H), 8.25 (m, 2H), 12.21 (bs, 1H). 13C NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 10.51, 105.83, 120.32, 125.17, 126.23, 128.19, 130.26, 132.61, 139.52, 166.34.

title: Discovery and Structure-Activity Relationships of Pyrrolone Antimalarials
authors: Murugesan, Dinakaran; Mital, Alka; Kaiser, Marcel; Shackleford, David M.; Morizzi, Julia; Katneni, Kasiram; Campbell, Michael; Hudson, Alan; Charman, Susan A.; Yeates, Clive; Gilbert, Ian H.
reference: Discovery and Structure-Activity Relationships of Pyrrolone Antimalarials | Murugesan, Dinakaran; Mital, Alka; Kaiser, Marcel; Shackleford, David M.; Morizzi, Julia; Katneni, Kasiram; Campbell, Michael; Hudson, Alan; Charman, Susan A.; Yeates, Clive; Gilbert, Ian H. | Journal of Medicinal Chemistry (2013), 56(7), 2975-2990
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: A. General procedure for the microwave-accelerated synthesis of 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrroles (6). 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. The vessel was placed in a microwave oven and heated (180 °C, 15-20 min) under microwave irradiation (0-400 W at 2.45 GHz). After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). 2,5-Dimethyl-1-(2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-1H-pyrrole (6a). Prepared following General Procedure A to give 6a. 3-(2,5-Dimethyl-1H-pyrrol-1-yl)pyridine (6r). Prepared following General Procedure A to give 6r as a dark-brown oil (2.8 g, 93%). 1H NMR (500 MHz, CDCl3): δ 8.50 (d, 1H, J = 1.5 Hz), 8.49 (d, 1H, J = 1.55 Hz), 8.38 (d, 1H, J = 2.05 Hz), 7.43 (m, 1H, J = 1.6 Hz), 5.79 (s, 2H), 1.89 (s, 6H). MS (ESI): calcd for C11H13N2, 173.1170; m/z found 173.1081 (M+1), 100%.

title: Paal-Knorr pyrrole synthesis using recyclable amberlite IR 120 acidic resin, a green approach

reference: Paal-Knorr pyrrole synthesis using recyclable amberlite IR 120 acidic resin, a green approach | Devi, Aarti; Shallu; Sharma, M. L.; Singh, Jasvinder | Synthetic Communications (2012), 42(10), 1480-1488
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure. A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (570 mg, 5 mmol), aniline (558 mg, 6 mmol), and amberlite IR 120 (200 mg) was stirred at room temperature under solvent-free conditions for 18 min. After completion of reaction, as monitered by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the reaction mixture was diluted with diethyl ether and filtered to recover the catalyst. The ether layer was washed with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine solution, dried (anhydrous Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by silica-gel column chromatography (eluting with 20% ethyl acetate in hexane). Pure product N-phenyl-2,5-dimethylpyrrole (846 mg) in 99% yield. The recovered catalyst was washed with 5% diluted HCl and dried prior to reuse. The IR spectrum of the recovered catalyst was identical to that of the commercially available catalyst, which was reused for further reactions (six times) without loss of activity. All the compounds are known and were identified by comparison with those of the authentic samples. 2,5-Dimethyl-1-(2-methylpropyl)-1H-pyrrole (Entry 15). Yield 99%. 1H NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 1.07 (d, 6H, J = 6.60 Hz), 2.17 (m, 1H), 2.36 (s, 6H), 3.67 (d, 2H, J = 6.60 Hz), 5.85 (s, 2H). 13C NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 11.33, 18.47, 28.39, 49.02, 104.09, 125.27.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the synthesis of compounds (3a-3s). 1-(4-Chloro-phenyl)-2, 5-dimethyl-1H-pyrrole (3a). A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (1, 1.0 mmol), 4-chlorophenylamine (2, 1.0 mmol), and α-amylase from hog pancreas (30 mg) was introduced to a test tube (10 mL), 2 mL CH3OH then the mixture was horizontally shake (160 rpm) at 50 °C. The solution was then filtered off by paper and the solvent was evaporated. The residue was purified by silica gel chromatography with an eluent consisting of petroleum/ethyl acetate (5:1 v/v). 1-Butyl-2,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrrole (3q); Yield: 95%; Liquid; Reaction condition: 2 h. IR (KBr) (νmax, cm-1): 2998, 1695, 1549, 1325, 1208. 1H-NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3): δ = 0.78-1.05 (m, 3H, CH3), 1.43-1.98 (m, 4H, CH2), 2.03 (s, 6H, CH3), 3.78-3.95 (m, 2H, CH2), 585 (s, 2H, CH).

reference: Discovery and Structure-Activity Relationships of Pyrrolone Antimalarials | Murugesan, Dinakaran; Mital, Alka; Kaiser, Marcel; Shackleford, David M.; Morizzi, Julia; Katneni, Kasiram; Campbell, Michael; Hudson, Alan; Charman, Susan A.; Yeates, Clive; Gilbert, Ian H. | Journal of Medicinal Chemistry (2013), 56(7), 2975-2990
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: A. General procedure for the microwave-accelerated synthesis of 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrroles (6). 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. The vessel was placed in a microwave oven and heated (180 °C, 15-20 min) under microwave irradiation (0-400 W at 2.45 GHz). After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). 2,5-Dimethyl-1-(2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-1H-pyrrole (6a). Prepared following General Procedure A to give 6a. 1-Benzyl-2,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrrole (6x). Prepared following General Procedure A to give 6x. Brown semi-solid, (2.9 g, 90%). 1H NMR (500 MHz, CDCl3): δ 7.41 (m, 3H, J = 7.45 Hz), 7.01 (d, 2H, J = 7.75 Hz), 5.98 (d, 2H, J = 10.6), 5.12 (d, 2H, J = 10.3. Hz), 2.25 (d, 6H, J = 10.4 Hz). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: A. General procedure for the microwave-accelerated synthesis of 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrroles (6). 2,5-Hexandione (4) (1 mmol), the appropriate aniline 5a-x (1.2 equiv) and p-toluenesulfonic acid bound with silica gel (0.4 equiv) were mixed in an oven dried pressure vial with a magnetic stirrer bar. After stirring for a further 15 min at room temperature the reaction mixture was filtered and the residual silica washed with DCM (10 mL). The solvent was removed under reduced pressure to give the corresponding 2,5-dimethyl-1-aryl-1H-pyrrole 6a-x (80-90% yield, purity >95% by LCMS). 2,5-Dimethyl-1-(2-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-1H-pyrrole (6a). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure. A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (570 mg, 5 mmol), aniline (558 mg, 6 mmol), and amberlite IR 120 (200 mg) was stirred at room temperature under solvent-free conditions for 18 min. After completion of reaction, as monitered by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the reaction mixture was diluted with diethyl ether and filtered to recover the catalyst. The ether layer was washed with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine solution, dried (anhydrous Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by silica-gel column chromatography (eluting with 20% ethyl acetate in hexane). Pure product N-phenyl-2,5-dimethylpyrrole (846 mg) in 99% yield. The recovered catalyst was washed with 5% diluted HCl and dried prior to reuse. The IR spectrum of the recovered catalyst was identical to that of the commercially available catalyst, which was reused for further reactions (six times) without loss of activity. All the compounds are known and were identified by comparison with those of the authentic samples. 1-(4-Bromophenyl)-2,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrrole (Entry 4). Yield 93%. Mp 75-76°C. 1H NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 1.99 (s, 6H), 5.78 (s, 2H), 7.06 (d, 2H), 7.55 (d, 2H). 13C NMR (300 MHz, CDCl3) δ 10.90, 104.46, 119.32, 125.90, 127.71, 130.07, 136.06.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure. A mixture of 2,5-hexadione (570 mg, 5 mmol), aniline (558 mg, 6 mmol), and amberlite IR 120 (200 mg) was stirred at room temperature under solvent-free conditions for 18 min. After completion of reaction, as monitered by thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the reaction mixture was diluted with diethyl ether and filtered to recover the catalyst. The ether layer was washed with saturated sodium bicarbonate solution and brine solution, dried (anhydrous Na2SO4), and concentrated in vacuo. The residue was purified by silica-gel column chromatography (eluting with 20% ethyl acetate in hexane). Pure product N-phenyl-2,5-dimethylpyrrole (846 mg) in 99% yield. The recovered catalyst was washed with 5% diluted HCl and dried prior to reuse. The IR spectrum of the recovered catalyst was identical to that of the commercially available catalyst, which was reused for further reactions (six times) without loss of activity. All the compounds are known and were identified by comparison with those of the authentic samples. 1-(2-Chlorophenyl)-2,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrrole (Entry 6). title: Successively Recycle Waste as Catalyst: A One-Pot Wittig/1,4-Reduction/Paal-Knorr Sequence for Modular Synthesis of Substituted Furans
authors: Chen, Long; Du, Yi; Zeng, Xing-Ping; Shi, Tao-Da; Zhou, Feng; Zhou, Jian
reference: Successively Recycle Waste as Catalyst: A One-Pot Wittig/1,4-Reduction/Paal-Knorr Sequence for Modular Synthesis of Substituted Furans | Chen, Long; Du, Yi; Zeng, Xing-Ping; Shi, Tao-Da; Zhou, Feng; Zhou, Jian | Organic Letters (2015), 17(6), 1557-1560
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the synthesis of trisubstituted furans 5a-v To a flame-dried schlenk tube were added phosphorane 1 (0.25 mmol, 1.0 eq) and symmetric 1,2-diketone 3 (0.25 mmol, 1.0 equiv). The tube was vacuumized and back-filled with N2, followed by the addition of 1.0 mL of anhydrous toluene. The resulting mixture was stirred at 120 °C for the time indicated in table 2 till almost full conversion of 1 by TLC analysis. After cooling to room temperature, the solvent was removed under reduced pressure and 1.0 mL of anhydrous ClCH2CH2Cl was added. Then HSiCl3 (58 mg, 45 uL, 0.5 mmol) was added in one portion and the reaction mixture was stirred vigorously. After the full conversion of the intermediate I by TLC analysis, two drops of MeOH was added into the resulting mixture and further vigorously stirring was needed to promote the transformation of the intermediate 1,4-diketone III to the furan product. Then the solvent was removed under reduced pressure, and the residue was directly subjected to flash column chromatograph using petroleum ether/ethyl acetate as the eluent. The desired product 5a-x. Column chromatography afforded the desired product 5l 18 in 70% yield (57.8 mg) as white solid. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3): δ 7.67-7.65 (m, 2H), 7.59-7.57 (m, 2H), 7.45-7.43 (m, 2H), 7.39-7.22 (m, 8H), 6.77 (s, 1H); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3): δ 151.42, 148.14, 134.01, 133.08, 130.84, 128.93, 128.68, 128.62, 128.41, 127.64, 127.37, 126.12, 124.94, 124.55, 109.84.
notes: green chemistry-waste reduction, one-pot Wittig/1,4-reduction/Paal-Knorr sequence, Ph3PO generated in stage 1 and HCl generated in stage 3 acting as catalysts, screw capped pressure tube used, toluene removed after stage 1
